subject: Re: OliveHealth pilot — packaging choices, upgrade/downgrade terms
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Moreno <sarah@olivetx.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: OliveHealth pilot — recommended packaging and questions

Sarah — thanks again for the demo last week. I promised a short note with a recommended packaging layout for the 3-month pilot and the options for scaling into a production contract. Attached is a one-page pack (OLIVE_PILOT_PACKAGING_v1.pdf) that summarizes the path. High level: 

- Pilot (3 months): Hosted API + a small Dedicated burst pool (2 reserved GPUs) for lower-latency endpoints and streaming experiments.
- Production options: A) Dedicated-first (reserved pool + hosted fallback) or B) Hosted-first (increase quota + optional Dedicated for steady throughput).

Open questions we need from your side to firm up pricing:
1) Expected concurrent streams for the RAG/Realtime demo (estimate: 50 concurrent streams = baseline).
2) Whether procurement needs a fixed monthly commitment for the pilot to issue a PO.
3) Any data residency constraint (EU region) for the pilot.

If procurement wants a pilot discount, we can propose a standard pilot concession (see suggested language) but we need to confirm whether unused committed capacity should convert to credits or be forfeited. Marcus and Ben — looping you for packaging/credits language and a fallback downgrade approach we can offer.

Next step: I'll wait for Sarah's answers then send a commercial term sheet and DocuSign link if Olive is ready.

—
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0123

Attachment: OLIVE_PILOT_PACKAGING_v1.pdf (1 page summary)
From: Sarah Moreno <sarah@olivetx.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurements@olivetx.com>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 11:08:00 -0800
Subject: Re: OliveHealth pilot — recommended packaging and questions

Marissa — thanks, that helps. A few clarifying points from my side so procurement can move quickly: 

- For the pilot we expect about 30–70 concurrent streams (bursty), so the dedicated pool makes sense.
- Procurement prefers not to sign large up-front monthly commitments for pilot projects; they usually accept a short term PO if there's a defined credit/offset for unused committed spend.
- We do have an EU data residency requirement for PHI-adjacent telemetry — pilot can run in US for experimentation, but production must support EU region.

Can you confirm: if we commit to a 2-GPU reserved pool for 3 months and only use 1 GPU worth of capacity on average, how does Redwood credit or refund that unused portion? Also, what are the upgrade/downgrade penalties if we go from Dedicated to Hosted-only after month 3?

Procurement is looped in (cc) and will respond with any PO timing constraints.

Thanks —
Sarah Moreno
Head of Integrations, OliveHealth
sarah@olivetx.com

Subject: Re: OliveHealth pilot — packaging choices (internal)

Marissa — quick internal note on how I'd approach the concessions and downgrade path. Quoted Sarah below for context.

Suggested commercial concessions (pilot-friendly):
- Pilot discount: 10% off standard hosted rates for 3 months.
- Dedicated burst: waive the first month of reserved pool fees (effectively 1 month free on the 3-month pilot for the 2-GPU pool).
- Unused committed capacity: convert unused reserved spend into platform credits at 75% of committed value, usable against hosted API usage for 12 months.

Upgrade/downgrade rules (proposal):
- Upgrade (Hosted -> Dedicated): effective immediately upon provisioning; billed pro-rata that month and then normal monthly billing.
- Downgrade (Dedicated -> Hosted-only): require 30 days' notice; remaining committed months converted to credits at the 75% rate above. No early termination fee beyond standard pro-rata.

Packaging layout (line items):
1) Pilot SKU: Hosted API (tier: Standard) — per-token pricing, 3-month pilot discount 10%
2) Dedicated burst: 2 x rtx-class GPUs reserved — list price + first month waived
3) Add-ons (optional): Persistent KV cache per-tenant, Priority streaming lane, 90-day telemetry retention (defaults to 30 days)

Numbers to include in the term sheet: monthly committed value for the 2-GPU pool (example: $18,000/mo for 2 GPUs) and the credit conversion math (unused_committed * 0.75 = credit). If they push for stronger concessions, propose a structured ramp: 10% pilot discount -> 7% recurring discount for first year if they convert to a 12-month Dedicated commit.

Marissa — happy to draft the commercial term sheet language. Ben, Laura — any compliance or billing caveats we should add (e.g., billing account separation for Hosted usage vs Dedicated commit)?

—Marcus
VP, Commercial
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Subject: OliveHealth — commercial term sheet and next steps

Sarah / Procurement — thanks for the quick replies. Per the internal suggestion from Marcus, attached is OLIVE_COMMERCIAL_TERM_SHEET_v2.docx with the specific line items and two commercial options (Hosted-first and Dedicated-first) plus the credit math for unused committed capacity. Highlights below so procurement can review quickly: 

Summary highlights (pilot):
- 3-month pilot (start Feb 1): Hosted Standard (10% pilot discount) + Dedicated burst: 2 reserved GPUs, monthly list $18,000, first month waived.
- Unused committed capacity conversion: unused_reserve_value * 0.75 = platform credit valid 12 months. Credits can be applied to Hosted usage or future Dedicated commits.
- Downgrade flexibility: 30 days notice, pro-rata billing for active month, remaining committed months converted to credits as above, no additional early termination fee.
- EU residency: we can provision production in EU region; pilot will be US-only unless Olive requests EU pilot. Production region selection added as a contract appendix.

Next steps: 
1) Procurement: please confirm PO timing and whether a short pilot PO is acceptable.
2) Sarah: please confirm the concurrent streams estimate (30–70) and whether you want the EU pilot option enabled now.
3) If agreed, we will send a DocuSign for the term sheet (link included below) and target a Feb 1 start.

DocuSign (preview): https://docusign.example.com/OLIVE-TS-2026
Deal record: https://app.redwood.com/deals/OLIVE-2026-P1

If procurement requests a lower upfront commitment in exchange for deeper first-year discounts, Marcus suggested a structured concession: 7% recurring discount for year 1 if they sign a 12-month Dedicated commit within 30 days of pilot completion.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

—
Marissa Cole | Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Marissa / Marcus — appreciate the clear options and the credit math. Procurement is comfortable with a short pilot PO if the unused-commitment crediting is documented the way you outlined. I have two remaining points before we sign: 

1) Hosted-only swap: if after month 3 we decide to move to Hosted-only, we want to confirm that we can do so without a surcharge beyond the credit conversion (i.e., no extra migration fee). Your term sheet language seems to say "no additional early termination fee" — can you confirm there isn't a one-time migration/setup fee for moving traffic off Dedicated?

2) EU residency appendix: please attach the EU region appendix you mentioned so our security team can review (we'll need SOC2 evidence + data residency clause).

If you can confirm item 1 in writing and attach the EU appendix, Procurement will share a pilot PO by EOD Friday. We are fine in principle with the 10% pilot concession + one month waived on Dedicated.

Thanks —
Sarah Moreno
Head of Integrations, OliveHealth
sarah@olivetx.com
